claims.statement: URE reported 1,544,574 grid-connected renewable microinstallations in Poland at year-end 2024, including 1,543,942 PV microinstallations and 1,522,655 prosumer-operated microinstallations.
More than two-thirds of prosumer microinstallations were connected to the PGE Dystrybucja and Tauron Dystrybucja networks at year-end 2024.

The national installed base and DSO-level concentration establish a large technical service surface, but they do not establish postcode-level incident density, installer portfolio density, or economical technician routes for the proposed launch zones.
UDT stated that its public register contained more than 9,500 certified renewable-system installers across Poland and exposed certificate validity information.

The UDT directory can support lawful prospecting, but a directory entry does not demonstrate spare calendar capacity, subcontracting willingness, insurance, current multi-brand competence, or permission to perform a particular warranty job.

IEA PVPS describes corrective maintenance as event-triggered work, treats response time as a contractible KPI, and notes that a more responsive corrective-maintenance programme can command a more expensive service price.

A response-window promise alone is a weak service contract: IEA PVPS recommends using response time in addition to outcome KPIs such as availability, yield, or performance, so the candidate would need an equivalent small-system resolution metric and clear exclusions.

IEA PVPS reports an approximately 11–12 year mean time between solar-inverter failures in cited multi-country studies and emphasizes that failure rates vary by product, installation quality, maintenance, and environment.

No public evidence was found that measures warranty callbacks, overflow incidents, or required field dispatches per 100 small or midsize Polish installer systems by product, postcode, season, and system age.

Where the installation seller is responsible for consumer-goods nonconformity, Polish consumer guidance says repair or replacement must occur within a reasonable time and the seller bears transport, labor, and material costs, creating a measurable callback-cost exposure.

Panasonic's Polish accreditation terms require its accredited heat-pump installer to diagnose a warranty defect within three business days and repair within two business days after parts arrive; missed duties permit Panasonic to commission an authorized service center at the installer's cost, and repeated misses can lead to immediate accreditation termination.

The Panasonic terms prove that at least one OEM channel can create an urgent, externally purchased service event borne by an installer, but they do not prove voluntary demand for this candidate's six-month reservation plus per-dispatch pricing.

Panasonic makes accreditation a binding relationship, requires continuing product training and compliance with its warranty procedures, and reserves substitute performance to its authorized service center, so covered heat-pump service rights are controlled by the OEM ecosystem rather than by generic OZE certification alone.

UDT states that an enterprise performing third-party installation, maintenance, service, repair, or decommissioning of stationary heat pumps containing fluorinated greenhouse gases must hold the relevant enterprise certificate.

Polish qualification rules cover maintenance, repair, installation, removal, and control-measurement work on regulated energy equipment; the stated small-equipment exception is limited to operation of specified electrical and thermal equipment, not a blanket exemption for repair work.

A dispatch pool must match each job to the right electrical qualification, F-gas enterprise/personnel coverage where applicable, and OEM-specific authority; technicians therefore cannot be treated as one freely interchangeable certified supply pool.

CS-OZE publicly offers installation companies outsourced post-sale monitoring, inspections, fault handling, and customer contact through nearby certified partners, explicitly offers to relieve overflow, and says the installer retains the commercial relationship while data terms are agreed in a DPA.

CS-OZE is a close Polish substitute addressing the same buyer, customer-relationship objection, dispatch workflow, and service categories, so the candidate does not possess an uncontested commercial control point.
CS-OZE recruits technicians by region and specialty, routes nearby prepared jobs, pays in a fixed cycle, imposes no exclusivity, and says each technician chooses how many jobs to accept.

The incumbent's nonexclusive, technician-choice model is a lower-commitment substitute for pre-reserved capacity; the candidate must prove that paying for reserved blocks produces enough SLA reliability to outweigh standby and utilization risk.

Otovo publicly offers Polish PV owners service memberships at 39, 109, and 199 PLN per month for 48-, 24-, and 12-hour response tiers; repairs are discounted rather than included, warranty handling and monitoring are included, and Otovo says most problems are resolved remotely.

Direct-to-owner subscriptions with remote triage give installers a referral or handoff alternative and may reduce field dispatch frequency, weakening a model whose margin depends on enough routed visits unless distinct B2B value is demonstrated.

Sunector's price list effective 1 August 2025 quotes 200 PLN net per hour for ordered heat-pump service plus 1.5 PLN per kilometer travel, 400–600 PLN net for annual PV inspection up to 20 kWp, and 200 PLN net for annual energy-storage inspection, excluding materials.

Observed retail service prices and separately charged travel leave uncertain room for a 250–600 PLN routing margin after technician pay, round-trip travel, failed visits, central triage, quality review, liability, credits, and parts coordination.

The government-commissioned Barometr Zawodów 2026 classifies electricians and energy workers as a nationwide deficit occupation and says recruiting appropriately qualified and willing workers can be difficult.

Technician scarcity can create buyer urgency but also increases reservation cost, refusal risk, and correlated peak-capacity failure, so it is not evidence that affordable standby blocks are obtainable.

No signed reservation, quote, or technician commitment establishes that unrelated qualified service firms will sell nonexclusive six-month postcode-and-response-window capacity blocks at a cost compatible with the proposed margins.
No unrelated installer letter of intent, prepayment, contract, or observed purchase establishes willingness to pay 900–2,500 PLN monthly plus a 250–600 PLN dispatch margin.

No evidence establishes cold outreach conversion, acquisition cost, onboarding time, churn, annual renewal, dispatch volume per subscribing installer, or geographic dispersion of subscribed portfolios.

No fully loaded contribution model is evidenced using observed incident rates, technician reservation prices, travel, rework, no-access visits, parts delays, warranty denial, insurance, dispatcher coverage, support time, credits, taxes, and correlated seasonal peaks.

No evidence establishes the candidate's lawful and practical access to end-customer data, inverter or battery telemetry, manufacturer portals, service histories, or warranty authority across brands without installer-specific data-processing, credential, and OEM arrangements.

No evidence establishes that standardized multi-brand triage will achieve a high first-visit resolution rate or that accumulated fault-code, route, and resolution data will be proprietary, permissioned, or more defensible than data held by manufacturers and existing service networks.

No operating evidence establishes that live dispatch, escalation, quality review, and customer support can be delegated while keeping the founder below five hours per day alongside full-time employment.

The evidence supports a real service surface, actual callback obligations, and paid work, but not the separate proposition that small and midsize installers form a large addressable overflow-reservation market.

No evidence supports the scale assumptions of 600 installer subscriptions, more than 12 million PLN annual revenue, or a resulting path to at least 5 million PLN of founder net worth; those outcomes remain contingent on unproven repeat economics and delegated operations.

contrary_evidence: CS-OZE already markets a close Polish substitute that takes over installer aftercare, preserves the installer's commercial relationship, and routes work to local certified technicians.
CS-OZE's technician-side offer is nonexclusive and lets technicians choose job volume, presenting a lower-commitment spot-network alternative to prepaid capacity blocks.
Otovo sells end owners monthly response-time memberships and says most issues are resolved remotely, which can bypass installers and suppress paid field dispatches.
Panasonic's accreditation terms place warranty procedure, service deadlines, and substitute-performance rights inside an OEM-controlled network rather than a generic multi-brand pool.
F-gas enterprise certification and electrical qualification rules fragment the legally eligible technician pool by task.
Electricians and energy workers are forecast as a nationwide deficit occupation in 2026, making affordable standby capacity less assured.
Public retail service prices plus explicit per-kilometer travel charges offer no demonstrated headroom for the proposed routing margin after all delivery and failure costs.

IEA PVPS reports that inverter failure rates are product-, installation-, maintenance-, and environment-dependent and cites an 11–12 year mean time between failures, so a large installed base alone cannot establish dense repeat dispatch demand.

unknowns: Field-worthy incident rate per 100 systems by installer, postcode, product, season, and system age.
Unrelated-installer willingness to prepay the proposed reservation fee and accept the dispatch markup.
Unrelated-technician willingness and price to commit six-month postcode-specific capacity with enforceable response windows.
Actual route density, round-trip kilometers, travel-time utilization, and simultaneous peak-event load in an initial service zone.
Manufacturer-by-manufacturer authorization, warranty acceptance, parts access, portal access, and reimbursement rules for subcontracted work.
Insurance cost, liability allocation, failed-visit credits, rework rate, no-access rate, and parts-delay exposure.
Cold acquisition conversion, CAC payback, onboarding burden, churn, renewal, and expansion revenue for unrelated installers.
First-visit resolution rate and the share of incidents resolved remotely without a paid dispatch.
Whether customer data and telemetry can be processed across installers and manufacturers on workable contractual terms.
Dispatcher and technical-escalation staffing needed to keep the founder within the five-hour daily limit.
Evidence that the operating model can reach hundreds of installer subscriptions and a founder-equity outcome consistent with the founder's wealth target.
